name: Split screen: bevelled split
when: The voice compares two places or things ("the street, and the track"). The default split. The first shot plays full frame, then the second slides in as a slanted panel and pushes it into the left half. Both shots play inside the scene; it ends on the split (cut to the next shot).
anchor: The panel (`in`) lands on the second name.

vars.shot1: the first shot: a 1920x1080 30 fps video in the project's assets/ (e.g. assets/footage/street.mp4), cut to start where it should start; it plays for the whole scene
vars.shot2: the second shot: a video in assets/, cut to start where it should start; it plays from `in` to the end
vars.label1: the first name, as the voice says it (shown in capitals, 9 characters at most)
vars.label2: the second name (9 characters at most)
vars.in: seconds after the start: when the voice says the second name (the panel slides in)
vars.out: seconds after the start: when the scene ends; it is a cut, so the scene lasts exactly `out`

changed: The shots are file values and play from their own start (cut each file where it should begin). The ground behind the scene is gone: the two shots always cover the frame.
